public_rationale: On 2026-03-01, Marcus forecast more military mistargeting incidents of the Minab type, and he gave no deadline. Reporting from September 2026 cites officials saying that over-reliance on Palantir's Maven system contributed to the Minab school strike (e1). That strike took place on 2026-02-28, before the post, so it is not a further incident. In March 2026, the Minab investigation had not been completed or published, and officials had then called an AI role unlikely (e2). Also in March 2026, a U.S. military spokesperson said the military had no way of knowing whether specific strikes used AI (e3). The packet contains no credible report of a mistargeting after 2026-03-01 that killed civilians and was attributed at least partly to AI. So the early-resolution rule is not met. With no deadline, the lack of such reports does not contradict the forecast. The forecast remains open.
limitations: The search did not cover every conflict in detail, for example Ukraine/Russia or Israel/Lebanon.
The Pentagon's Minab report had not been officially published in the sources found.
The packet does not show whether AI was used in strikes after the post, and finding no reports does not show that no such incident happened.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There will be more AI-related military mistargeting incidents like the one in Iran.

statement.excerpt: The second is: we can certainly expect incidents of this type, and more of them.
statement.document_title: Is AI already killing people by accident?

from_speaker: we can certainly expect incidents of this type
'this type' refers to a military mistargeting that kills civilians and may involve AI
our_interpretation: Read as a forecast that more military mistargeting incidents will happen after the post, where AI plays a role and civilians die.
No deadline was given, so the horizon is open. The forecast can be settled early only by a decisive dated event.
Repeated incidents count only if AI is credibly reported as a contributing cause. Ordinary targeting errors do not count, because Marcus himself notes that 'targeting errors aren't new'.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reporting names at least one military mistargeting incident after 2026-03-01 that killed civilians and had AI as a contributing cause. This could be an official investigation, or a major news outlet citing officials or documents.
criteria.contradiction_condition: With no deadline, nothing short of an implausibly long period without such incidents could contradict it. In practice the forecast cannot be shown false within the evaluation window.

evidence.excerpt: artificial intelligence embedded in the Maven Smart System owned by Palantir Technologies Inc., contributed to the disaster
evidence.explanation: Officials later linked the original Minab strike partly to AI over-reliance. That strike happened before the post, so it is not a further incident of the kind forecast.

evidence.excerpt: The investigation is reportedly examining whether the error originated in human analytical failure, an AI-assisted geospatial targeting system (although officials have said this is unlikely), or some combination of the two.
evidence.explanation: Shows that attributing even the original incident to AI was disputed and unresolved for months. This makes later attributions hard to establish.

evidence.excerpt: The U.S. military has “no way of knowing” whether it used artificial intelligence in conducting specific airstrikes
evidence.explanation: The military says it cannot tell which strikes used AI, so further AI-linked incidents may never be publicly confirmed.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An official investigation, a reputable news report citing officials or documents, or an independent monitor such as Airwars attributing a military mistargeting after 2026-03-01 that killed civilians at least partly to an AI system or to reliance on one.
